event_text: Citizens of Leeuwarden, Netherlands, strike against a ban on foreign beer.
headline: Leeuwarden Beer Riot Erupts in 1487
story: Barry peered over the rooftops, watching as the citizens of Leeuwarden marched through the streets. 'Seems the city council's imposed a ban on foreign beer, Susan. Locals aren't having it – they're rather fond of their imported ale.' Susan cocked her head. 'Can't say I blame them. I mean, have you tried the local brew? Tastes like someone's washed their socks in it.' Barry snorted. 'Well, the protesters are certainly making their point – they've already overturned a few market stalls and are now heading for the council chambers.' Susan ruffled her feathers. 'I do hope they're not planning on storming the place – those council members can be a bit...prickly. Still, it's hard to argue with the sentiment – who doesn't love a good pint of foreign beer?' The protest, it seemed, was all about the right to choose one's own brew, rather than being forced to drink the local swill. As the crowd surged forward, Barry and Susan watched with interest, wondering how the city council would respond to this sudsy uprising.
regret_line: They should have just stuck to drinking the local brew – it's not like it was going to kill them or anything.
winner_line: The local tavern owners, who likely saw a significant increase in sales of their own, admittedly dubious, ale.
